text:
I called my wife at work and asked, "Do you ever get a shooting pain across your body, like someone's got a voodoo doll of you and they're stabbing it?" Sounding concerned, she said, "No."
I responded, "How about now?"
gist: A husband calls his wife asking about voodoo-doll stabbing pains, and when she says no he asks 'how about now?', revealing he has the doll.

text:
I used to sell security alarms door to door, and I was really good at it.
If no one was home,  I would just leave a brochure on the kitchen table.
gist: A door-to-door alarm salesman brags he was great at it because when nobody was home he left a brochure on the kitchen table, revealing he broke in.

text:
The son went to his dad and asked him, "Dad, what's an alcoholic?"
So the dad replied, "Do you see those four trees? Well, an alcoholic would see eight."
The son replied, "But Dad, I only see two."
gist: A father explains an alcoholic sees double by pointing at four trees, and his son replies there are only two, revealing the father is drunk.

text:
Wife: “I’m pregnant.”
Me: “Hi Pregnant, I’m Dad.”
Wife: “No you’re not.”
gist: A husband answers his wife's pregnancy news with the dad-joke greeting Hi Pregnant, I'm Dad, and she replies that he is not, implying he isn't the father.

wordplay.explanation: 'Hi X, I'm Dad' dad-joke formula; 'No you're not' turns 'I'm Dad' into a literal paternity denial.

adaptNote: dad-joke formula unknown, short adjective 'beremenna' awkward as a name

text:
I was going to donate blood today, but they always ask waaaay too many personal questions
Like, "who's blood is this", and "where did you get it?"
gist: Would-be blood donor complains the clinic asks too many personal questions, and the questions reveal he is bringing someone else's blood, implying murder.

text:
I finally realized my parents favored my twin brother.
It hit me when they asked me to blow up balloons for his surprise birthday party.
gist: Man realizes his parents favor his twin brother when they ask him to blow up balloons for the twin's surprise birthday party, which is also his own birthday.

text:
A guy sits down in a diner and asks for a bowl of hot chili...
The waitress says, "Sorry, but the guy next to you got the last bowl".
He looks over and sees that the guy's finished his meal, but the bowl of chili is still full. He asks, "Are you going to eat that chili?"
The other guy says, "No. Help yourself".
He slides the bowl of chili over and starts to eat. When he gets about half way down, his spoon hits something. He looks down sees a dead mouse and immediately pukes all the chili back into the bowl.
The other guy says, "Yeah, that's about as far as I got, too".
gist: A diner eats a stranger's untouched chili, finds a dead mouse halfway and vomits back into the bowl, and the stranger says that's as far as he got too.
